summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge: analyze Soony's confidential launch data, find where SAP and supplier documents disagree, and build an agent product that detects, explains with sources, and acts (emails, calls, Teams alerts).
summary.outcome: Found real launch risks (overbooked art books, failed statues, game cards offloaded, sleeve revision conflict) and built a poller/versioned store, evidence anchoring with local OCR, redesigned evidence panel, Teams webhook alerts and a Monty-sandbox routines MVP. Briefing page and Felix interview doc were also created. Several commits remain unpushed and the Teams webhook is not yet configured.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no notifications or webhooks; files get replaced under the same name, so change detection must poll and compare SHA-256.
Confidential portal data lives in the gitignored data/ folder, and .env is gitignored while .env.example is committed.
Team workflow is defined in CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md, and tasks are claimed with a 'Now' line in PROGRESS.md.
Verifier builds a link graph in code (order, confirmation, shipment, receipt, scan); state is JSON files in data/state/ plus SQLite for watcher file versions and alerts.

The card builder in dispatch/decisions flattens evidence into plain strings, losing file and page references; it is owned by the verifier pipeline authors and has a HANDOFF.md, so coordinate before changing it.
Several modules writing the same JSON file caused a dict vs list conflict in actions.json.
Some tests were loading the real .env (including the password) and only passed due to test order; now isolated by running every test in an empty folder via conftest.
Anchoring indexes 320 portal files in about 36 s using PDF text positions, tesseract OCR for scans and table rows; tesseract was added to the Dockerfile.
Monty (pydantic-monty) runs agent-written Python in a sandbox that can call only whitelisted functions; type-checking rejects wrong calls before execution.

code.finding: Generic anchoring: normalizes numbers/IDs ('56.000' = '56,000'), matches evidence to PDF words, OCR boxes and table rows, with a ranking heuristic that can pick less fitting sources for common numbers.
One-way Teams Adaptive Card via Workflows webhook with system-vs-document columns and buttons into /d/<id>; first run only records existing cards to avoid flooding.
Routines MVP: agent writes short code from a whitelist of building blocks and runs it in the Monty sandbox, with an on/off switch in the UI.
Evidence viewer that shows the PDF page or scan with yellow markers, or a table with the marked row.

workflow: A subagent was effective for cross-checking 200 order confirmations and 59 scans in parallel against SAP.
Screenshots via headless Chrome let the assistant verify UI before handing it over.
Entire only creates checkpoints when repo files change, so read-only sessions show no checkpoint.
Asking before pushing and merging to shared branches was the working pattern, since commits stayed unpushed pending the user's OK.
Check licences (n8n Sustainable Use License) before building a product on a tool.

friction: Portal token was initially empty, blocking data access until the user supplied it.
Data drops arrive unannounced during the hack, so the 14:00 analysis went stale by 14:37 and the doc and page still show the old state.
A stray other-session change to basic_auth.py reverted a favicon commit and had to be discarded.
Test isolation bug: my Teams commit briefly broke tests because the real .env leaked into them.
OCR for scans required debugging the tesseract subprocess call and TSV output, plus deduping split-word boxes.
The Routines button overlapped the map legend and had to be moved.
The procurementmag article blocked automated access.
Unclear whether portal data and supplier replies differ per team.
